newsitem.title: INDIA: NZ SPORT - Cairns to bowl, newcomers set to debut.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT - Cairns to bowl, newcomers set to debut.

text.p: HYDERABAD, May 20 - New Zealand are set to press Chris Cairns into service as a bowler after a three-month break for their crucial Independence Cup series one-day cricket match against Sri Lanka at Lal Bahadur Stadium on Tuesday night (NZ time).
NZPA reports Cairns has not bowled for three months because of an ankle injury, which is due to be operated on next month.

He was selected for this tournament solely as a specialist batsman, but will be used as the sixth bowler tonight as New Zealand make tactical and personnel changes for their final preliminary match in the four-nation competition.
"We want him to bowl four or five overs off a shortened run in this game," Kiwi captain Stephen Fleming said of Cairns.
Fleming and coach Steve Rixon, contemplating their likely 11 to take on the World Cup holders, asked Cairns to bowl four overs off a reduced run at training yesterday.
He did so, and Fleming and Rixon are now convinced he can play a part with the ball in a game where victory would carry New Zealand into the best-of-three final against either India or Pakistan.

Expecting Cairns to play even a small role with the ball seems to be a desperate measure from the New Zealand management, but Fleming said his availability as a sixth bowling option suited the balance of the team they wanted to take into the game.
"It was a call made by Steve and myself. We see this match as a one-off situation. We have to win it to make the final."

New Zealand are not due to confirm their 11 until late this afternoon (NZ time) but are expected to vary their gameplan and use offspinner Dipak Patel to open the attack alongside raw Otago left arm seamer Shayne O'Connor, who looks sure to be
called in to make his debut with another newcomer, Canterbury batsman Craig McMillan.

Fast-medium bowlers Heath Davis and Andrew Penn should be discarded after proving to be very expensive in the two earlier games, while McMillan's presence is needed to strengthen an under-performed middle order.

"Chris has agreed that he can do it for us, but he is a little bit worried by what the perception may be from New Zealand Cricket, Nottinghamshire officials in England and supporters at home because he hasn't been able to bowl for so long," Fleming said.
Cairns chipped a bone in his left ankle in February. It pains him in his delivery stride when bowling but does not affect him when batting or fielding.

He delayed the operation until after the Independence Cup series which meant Nottinghamshire released him from his county contract this year as they sought the services of another overseas fast bowler.

Team physiotherapist Mark Plummer said Cairns should not suffer any permanent damage by bowling. It would be painful for him, but the damage had already been inflicted and would be repaired when he underwent the operation.
Fleming said the special circumstances surrounding this match, and the anticipated changes to the bowling personnel, prompted an approach being made to Cairns to don his bowling boots again.
"The call was made by me and Steve merely to give us more security on the bowling front. If we win this match we are through to the final. It is a last ditch match," he said.
"For the good of the balance of the team we want we needed to know he could bowl four or five overs off a short run if required."
The reshaping of the new ball attack comes as no surprise after Davis and Penn proved very expensive in the earlier preliminary matches against Pakistan and India.
O'Connor, 23, will fully deserve his promotion. He has impressed at training and his partnership with Patel is a sign of flexibility in the team management's approach.
They had previously become glued to the concept of attacking with pace at either end in the early overs in the hope of nicking out two or three opposition batsmen.
The ploy has not worked because Penn and Davis were wayward in direction and found no assistance whatsoever on the flat Indian tracks.

Patel's initial overs to dangerous Sri Lankan opener Sanath Jayasuriya will be intriguing. Jayasuriya, who scored 151 not out against India on Sunday morning (NZ time), likes to use the pace of the ball off the pitch to hit square on both sides of his legs.

Patel has opened the attack only once before during Rixon's reign as coach which will extend to 18 one-day internationals after this match. But he has previously performed well in that role, particularly during the 1992 World Cup tournament.
"We haven't bowled well in the early overs in the last two games and the pitches here have not helped out quicker bowlers," Fleming said.
"It'd be stupid to be pig-headed and carry on with a philosophy that isn't working."
O'Connor faces a tall order to Jayasuriya under control, but does not appear fazed by the challenge.
"If I play here I will have a job to do and I just have to forget about who I am bowling to. All I want to think about is landing the ball in the right spot," O'Connor said.
"What I don't want to happen is for me to have a bad game and for people to come up to me afterwards and say 'it's your first game and you're allowed to do that'.
"I'd rather just go out there and do my job properly."
Concerns over the fitness of medium pacer Gavin Larsen have eased after he bowled unhindered for 40 minutes at three-quarter to full pace yesterday.
Larsen sustained a calf muscle strain in Bangalore last week when New Zealand lost to India and it was initially feared he would not be fit to take on Sri Lanka.
But he has made a pleasing recovery, though his fitness will again be gauged before New Zealand confirm their team.
Teams:
New Zealand (likely): Stephen Fleming (captain), Nathan Astle, Bryan Young, Matt Horne, Chris Cairns, Chris Harris, Craig McMillan, Adam Parore, Dipak Patel, Gavin Larsen and Shayne O'Connor.

Sri Lanka (from): Arjuna Ranatunga (captain), Sanath Jayasuriya, Roshan Mahanama, Marvan Atapattu, Aravinda de Silva, Hashan Tillekaratne, Romesh Kaluwitharana, Chaminda Vaas, Muttiah Muralitharan, Kumar Dharmasena, Sajeewa de Silva, Upul Chandana, Ruwan Kalpage and Dulip Liyange.
